lines.trans: Just don't worry, everything will be fine.
You are a real beauty!
Thanks, Mom! Well how is it, Slavik?
Of course it's good for you, you're the troubadour!
Try putting on the donkey costume yourself.
I offered to let you be the rooster.
And I actually wanted to be the cat!
And who will loudly crow then?
Why must I scream from the stage?
Slavik, you are always dissatisfied with everything!
You never like anything.
Soon our amateur talent evening will begin.
We will sing the Bremen musicians' song.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.
Nothing lasts forever under the moon.
I have no idea at all.

meanings.note: at the start of a sentence
поставить громко = to put a phone on speaker

examples.text: Не говорите так громко, дети спят.
examples.trans: Don't speak so loudly, the children are asleep.

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

meanings.note: как вы знаете = as you know

examples.trans: This is my wedding suit, actually!

meanings.note: кошка is the general / female word

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
to put on (an item of clothing)

examples.trans: He put on his best suit.

начаться.gloss: to begin, to start, to break out

meanings.en: to begin, to start, to break out (intransitive)

examples.trans: The film started at seven sharp.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось
the person who likes is in the dative: мне нравится = I like it
hesitation, at the start of a sentence

examples.trans: This is my favourite old song.

meanings.en: to try, to taste (food or drink)

examples.trans: Try the tea with bread rings.
Why are we going so slowly?

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми
спасибо за + accusative = thank you for
выйти на сцену = to go out on stage

meanings.en: scene (in a play, film, or argument)

examples.text: А на сцену выходит — превращается в дерево.
examples.trans: But when she goes out on stage, she turns into a tree.
The actors came out onto the stage.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
